root_cause.text: The `max_register` field in the regmap configuration was set to the size of the register memory region (65536) instead of the offset of the last valid register (65532), causing out-of-bounds register reads that trigger a kernel page fault when accessed via debugfs.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "The max_register field is assigned the size of the register memory region instead of the offset of the last register." The patch changes `.max_register = XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN` to `.max_register = XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET`, where `XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET` is defined as `(XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN - 4)`. The crash trace shows a translation fault at address `ffff800082f70000`, which is beyond the valid register range, confirming the out-of-bounds access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Define a macro for the maximum valid register offset to enable bounds checking.
intent_record.what: Added macro XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET defined as (XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN - 4), which equals 65532.
intent_record.how: This macro provides a constant representing the maximum valid byte offset into the XDMA register space, assuming 4-byte registers. It can be used for bounds checking to prevent out-of-bounds register accesses.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix regmap max_register boundary to use the maximum register offset instead of the register space length, preventing out-of-bounds register accesses.
intent_record.what: Changed the value of the `.max_register` field in the regmap_config struct from `XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN` to `XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET`.
intent_record.how: The `max_register` field sets the highest valid register offset for the regmap. Using `XDMA_REG_SPACE_LEN` (the total size in bytes) would allow accesses beyond the last valid register, while `XDMA_MAX_REG_OFFSET` (presumably the maximum offset, equal to size-1) correctly restricts access to the legitimate register range.
